sample.answer: {"replacement":"function page(rows, tenant, offset, limit) { const start = Math.max(0, offset); const count = Math.max(0, limit); return rows.filter(row => row.tenant === tenant && !row.deleted).sort((a, b) => a.created < b.created ? -1 : a.created > b.created ? 1 : a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0).slice(start, start + count).map(row => row.id); }","explanation":"The current implementation slices before filtering, allowing other tenants or deleted rows to consume page positions, and lacks the required id tie-breaker. This replacement filters exact tenant matches and excludes truthy deleted rows before sorting. It orders by created, then by id using JavaScript string comparisons, not locale-sensitive collation. Filtering and sorting use a new array, leaving the input array and row objects unchanged. Negative offset and limit are clamped to zero; slicing after ordering handles zero limits and offsets beyond eligible rows. The example’s red rows order c, b, d, so offset 1 and limit 2 return b, d."}

{"replacement":"function summarize(items, config) { const active = items.filter(item => !item.cancelled); if (active.length === 0) return { subtotal: 0, discount: 0, shipping: 0, total: 0 }; const subtotal = active.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.cents * item.qty, 0); const discount = Math.floor(subtotal * config.discountBps / 10000); const net = subtotal - discount; const shipping = net >= config.freeShippingAt ? 0 : config.shippingCents; return { subtotal, discount, shipping, total: net + shipping }; }","explanation":"The implementation counts cancelled rows in subtotal, although the billing contract says to ignore them. It rounds the discount instead of flooring it, applies shipping unconditionally rather than comparing net with freeShippingAt, and computes total from undiscounted subtotal. It also returns nonzero shipping for an empty invoice, while the contract requires every result field to be zero when no active rows remain. The replacement filters without changing input rows and reads all three policy values from the supplied config, so it works beyond the sample settings."}

{"replacement":"function summarize(items, config) { let subtotal = 0; let hasActiveRows = false; for (const item of items) { if (item.cancelled) continue; hasActiveRows = true; subtotal += item.cents * item.qty; } if (!hasActiveRows) return { subtotal: 0, discount: 0, shipping: 0, total: 0 }; const discount = Math.floor(subtotal * config.discountBps / 10000); const net = subtotal - discount; const shipping = net >= config.freeShippingAt ? 0 : config.shippingCents; return { subtotal, discount, shipping, total: net + shipping }; }","explanation":"The existing implementation includes cancelled rows, rounds the discount instead of flooring it, always charges shipping, and calculates total from the undiscounted subtotal. This replacement sums only active rows, computes the discount with Math.floor, derives net before applying the configured free-shipping threshold, and totals net plus shipping. It returns four zero fields when the input has no active rows, including an empty array or all-cancelled rows. It reads each supplied config value directly, uses no defaults or mutation, and leaves every input row unchanged."}
